claims.text: Home Office accepts only an approved-provider SELT for most UK visas needing English
claims.quote: For most UK visas that ask for English, the Home Office accepts only a Secure English Language Test (SELT) from an approved provider.

passage.text: University and study abroad Immigration and visas Citizenship Work and careers Healthcare professionals School and young learners Other useful tests Visas: you need an approved SELT For most UK visas that ask for English, the Home Office accepts only a Secure English Language Test (SELT) from an approved provider. You must take it at an approved test location, and you must receive the result within two years before you apply. As of September 2026, the approved tests are:

passage.text: at an approved test location, and you must receive the result within two years before you apply. claims.text: Degree-level Student visa needs CEFR B2
claims.quote: For degree-level study on a Student visa you need English at CEFR B2.

passage.text: PTE Academic practice tests prepare you for them. We do not offer practice for LanguageCert, Trinity, Skills for English, PTE Home or IELTS Life Skills. Studying at a UK university For degree-level study on a Student visa you need English at CEFR B2. You can prove it with a SELT, but a university that is a Higher Education Provider may also assess your English itself. This is why universities can accept tests that are not SELTs, such as TOEFL iBT, the Duolingo English Test or Cambridge C1 Advanced. For study below degree level, the requirement is B1 and a SELT is normally needed. Always check your university's list.

contradictions.assessment: Source 8 (Sept 2026, cites gov.uk) says not a SELT; source 3 (single source) says added in 2026. Treat as not a SELT until confirmed on GOV.UK.

IELTS UKVI result must be under 12 months old at application

contradictions.assessment: Source 8 says two years for SELTs; source 3 says 12 months for IELTS only. Unverified; confirm on GOV.UK.

PTE Academic UKVI results typically take 7-10 working days

contradictions.assessment: Undated source 1 says 48 hours; source 3 says 7-10 working days. Neither corroborated.

recommendation.headline: IELTS for UKVI (Academic) for the widest acceptance; PTE Academic UKVI if speed matters more and your university accepts it
recommendation.summary: IELTS for UKVI is an approved SELT with the widest recognition. Speed evidence for UKVI tests is conflicting and thin.

reasons.text: Approved SELT and broadest recognition (13,500 vs ~3,000 organisations).
Sheffield accepts all IELTS for postgraduate entry.
Paper or computer choice; UKVI version same content as standard IELTS.

tradeoffs.text: No source verifies IELTS result speed; PTE may be faster but UKVI turnaround is disputed.

alternatives.when: Speed is the top priority and your university accepts PTE.
Only if your university explicitly accepts it; do not rely on it as a SELT.

caveats: Sources 3 and 8 disagree on Duolingo SELT status and IELTS validity; source 8 preferred.
Most sources are commercial or undated.
